> 坤。元亨，利牝馬之貞。

If 乾 is rising energy, 坤 is usually taught as its opposite: earth, yielding, the female, stillness.

The character says something more specific, and the stillness part is the mistake.

## 坤 was 川 written sideways

坤's early form is 巛 — 川 laid on its side. Warring States texts use it constantly, and the Mawangdui 易 writes 坤 simply as 川. The 土 radical comes later.

So the picture inside 坤 is three streams running downward, in order, not disputing the channel.

說文 glosses 坤 as 地, but that gloss is based on the later form with 土. The older shape gives the more useful reading: 坤 is 順 — compliance that is not static, but a flow.

## 牝馬: why a horse and not a cow

牝 is the female of a domestic animal, from 牛 and 匕.

But the text says 牝馬 — female horse. Why a horse?

Because a horse is compliant and can go far. A cow is compliant and slow. A horse is compliant and covers distance.

So 坤's 貞 is not "not moving." It is: following, and able to go the distance while following.

This is the layer most readings lose. 坤 is not rest. It is load-bearing motion.

## 含章

章: 樂竟為一章 — the original sense is a piece of music finishing; from that, "pattern," "what shows."

So 含章 is holding something that could show, and not letting it.

含, as in chapter 55 of the Daodejing, is to keep something in the mouth — neither swallowed nor spat.

Water flowing and not loud: the image and the character agree.

## 括囊

括: 絜也 — to bind, to tie up.

括囊 is tying the mouth of the sack shut.

The precision matters: tied, not torn. The sack is intact; it has simply stopped opening. That is 藏, not 毀.

## 玄黃

玄 is the color of the sky; 黃 the color of the earth.

龍戰於野，其血玄黃 — the blood is dark and yellow.

This is the harshest image in the two chapters. Injury here is not "bleeding." It is colors mixing: sky-color and earth-color poured together until you cannot tell which is which.

## 永貞

The 用六 line: 用六，永貞.

永 is duration; 貞 is what is kept.

And here 乾 and 坤 use the same character differently: 乾's 貞 is what was asked (貞，卜問也), 坤's 貞 is what is held.

One character, two uses — which is exactly what the 系辭 means by 不可為典要: the text cannot be turned into a fixed glossary.

## A test

Take something you are carrying — a role, a household, a long project. Ask whether you are holding it still or carrying it forward. 坤 is the second, and the difference shows up in whether the thing has moved in a year.
